Amanda Crego-Emley, Assistant Professor and Head of Reference, University Libraries Amanda joined the URI Libraries faculty in 2023 and has been actively involved in university service, viewing shared governance as an essential part of building partnerships and strengthening campus community. In her first year, she served on the Academic Affairs Artificial Intelligence Task Force where she helped gather and amplify faculty perspectives about AI’s implications for teaching and learning at URI. Later, she joined the Faculty Senate, where she has spent two years serving on the General Education Committee. She is committed to advancing equity and access and supporting faculty research and teaching needs across the university. If elected, she will bring a cross-disciplinary perspective and a collaborative approach to the Executive Committee. As an Assistant Professor and Head of Reference in the URI Libraries, Amanda supports students, faculty, and staff across departments. She manages the library’s Research Help Desk, coordinates reference services, and supervises a team of Reference Graduate Student Assistants. She teaches a credit-bearing general education course and provides course-integrated information literacy instruction guided by active learning and inclusive pedagogy. Because the library serves all of URI, Amanda is deeply committed to building strong relationships with faculty and students, understanding shared campus challenges, and advocating for faculty concerns that transcend disciplinary divisions.
